page_0.title: Automation Exercise
page_0.summary:
- Main purpose: an e-commerce demo site for functional and automation practice (browse products, filter by category/brand, manage cart, signup/login, and try sample APIs/tutorials).
- Main user flows: navigate top menu (Home, Products, Cart, Signup/Login, Test Cases, Contact us, API Testing, Video Tutorials), browse category tree (WOMEN/MEN/KIDS and subcategories), filter by brands, view/add products to cart, and user authentication/checkout flows.
- Secondary flows: access "APIs list for practice" and "Test Cases"/tutorial pages for learning and API testing.
- Key UI actions to test: menu navigation, category/brand filtering, product listing/detail pages, add/remove items in cart, signup/login form behavior, contact form submission, link/button responsiveness.
- Data/state edge cases: empty cart, cart persistence across sessions, product quantity limits, out-of-stock items, and mismatched brand counts (numbers next to brands).
- Input validation edge cases: signup/login with invalid emails, weak passwords, SQL/HTML/JS injection, very long strings, and special/unicode characters (e.g., " Products" encoding).
- Navigation/links edge cases: duplicated nav items (two "Test Cases"), hidden or duplicate anchor elements, broken links, and incorrect redirects.
- Concurrency/security edge cases: simultaneous cart updates, session timeout, CSRF/auth token handling, and unauthorized access to restricted pages.
- Accessibility/responsiveness: keyboard navigation, ARIA/alt text presence, screen-reader flow, and layouts on mobile/tablet breakpoints.

page_1.title: Automation Exercise - All Products
page_1.summary:
- Main purpose: list all products so users can browse by category/brand, view product details, and add items to the shopping cart.
- Main user flows: navigate site via header (Home, Products, Cart, Signup/Login, Contact); filter/browse by category (WOMEN/MEN/KIDS) and brand; open "View Product" for details; "Add to cart" then "View Cart"; use #scrollUp to return to top.
- Authentication flow: separate Signup / Login page — verify behavior for actions when user is logged out vs logged in.
- Filters & counts: brand items show counts (e.g., POLO (6)) — expect filters to update visible products.
- Cart interactions: adding items, repeated adds (quantity aggregation), viewing cart and persistence across page reloads/sessions.
- UI/behavior edge cases: broken/missing images or links, "View Product" modal vs page navigation differences, stale or incorrect product counts.
- Concurrency & data integrity: stock changes between view and add-to-cart, race conditions when multiple adds/checkout attempts occur.
- Performance & error handling: slow network/timeouts, pagination or lazy-load behavior, and empty-result states when filters return no products.

page_2.title: Automation Exercise - Checkout
page_2.summary:
- Main purpose: display the shopping cart/checkout view so users can review items and proceed to purchase or navigate elsewhere on the site.
- Primary user flows: view/edit cart contents (quantities, remove items), navigate to Home/Products/Cart/Signup-Login/Test Cases/API Testing/Video Tutorials/Contact via top links, proceed to checkout, and subscribe to newsletter (input #susbscribe_email + button #subscribe).  
- Secondary flows: use the "here" link (contextual redirection) and use the #scrollUp control to return to top.
- Important state flows: guest vs. logged-in checkout (different redirects or prompts), cart persistence across page reloads/sessions, and concurrent updates from multiple tabs/devices.
- Input validation: newsletter email format validation, handling duplicate subscriptions, and proper success/error messaging.
- Quantity/contents edge cases: zero, negative, extremely large quantities, removing last item (empty cart), and applying changes without page refresh.
- Navigation/link edge cases: broken links, wrong redirects for "here" or signup/login, and keyboard/ARIA accessibility for anchors and buttons.
- Robustness/network edge cases: server timeouts, slow responses, partial failures when updating cart or subscribing, and retry/error states.
- UI/interaction edge cases: unclickable elements due to overlays, misplaced z-index, race conditions between rapid clicks, and responsive layout issues on small screens.

page_3.title: Automation Exercise - Signup / Login
page_3.summary:
- Main purpose: allow users to sign up or log in, subscribe to a newsletter, and navigate to site sections (Products, Cart, Contact, Test Cases, API Testing, Video Tutorials).
- Main user flows: user login, user signup/registration, newsletter subscription (email input + subscribe), site navigation via header links, access Cart/Products, and use scrollUp.
- Expected controls: Login and Signup buttons, subscribe button, email input for subscription, various nav anchors.
- Important functional checks: successful and failed login (valid/invalid creds), signup with valid/invalid/duplicate data, email validation for subscription, required-field/empty-input behavior.
- Input edge cases: very long strings, leading/trailing whitespace, special characters, SQL/XSS payloads, Unicode/emoji in fields.
- State/session edge cases: authentication persistence, logout behavior, redirect to protected pages when unauthenticated, concurrent sessions.
- UI/UX edge cases: buttons disabled/enabled states, error/success message visibility and content, layout/responsiveness, scrollUp behavior.
- Robustness/performance: behavior on slow network, rapid repeated submissions (rate limiting), retry after server errors.
- Security/validation: client-side vs server-side validation mismatch, CSRF token absence, improper error information leakage.

page_4.title: Automation Practice for API Testing
page_4.summary:
- Main purpose: a practice catalog page listing API endpoints (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) for learners to test and exercise API requests against Automation Exercise.
- Main user flows: site navigation (Home, Products, Cart, Signup/Login, Test Cases, API Testing, Video Tutorials, Contact us); selecting an API entry to view endpoint details; executing requests for endpoints like Get All Products, Search Product, Verify Login, Create/Register, Update/Delete user.
- Typical tester actions: click each API link, submit/inspect GET/POST/PUT/DELETE calls, follow base URLs, and exercise signup/login flows tied to APIs.
- Important functional checks: correct HTTP method enforcement, correct status codes and response bodies for valid vs invalid input, and that endpoint links resolve to the documented URL.
- Auth/side‑effect edge cases: endpoints requiring authentication (login/register), idempotency and state cleanup for POST/DELETE/PUT, repeated deletes or updates on non‑existent resources.
- Input validation edge cases: empty fields, malformed JSON, extremely long strings, special characters, SQL/JS injection payloads, and incorrect content‑type headers.
- Resilience/network edge cases: slow responses/timeouts, partial responses, 4xx/5xx error handling, and unexpected HTML or redirect responses from the listed https://automationexercise.com links.
- UI/content edge cases: truncated/garbled API labels (seen in elements), broken/mislinked API entries, missing descriptions, and accessibility of each navigation item.

page_5.title: Automation Exercise - Contact Us
page_5.summary:
- Main purpose: a Contact Us page to let users send messages to the site team and to subscribe to the newsletter/contact list.
- Main user flows: submit contact form (populate inputs + textarea #message → submit → expect success/error feedback); subscribe by entering email in input #susbscribe_email and clicking button #subscribe; navigate to other site areas via top links (Home, Products, Cart, Signup / Login, Test Cases, API Testing, Video Tutorials, Contact us); click feedback@automationexercise.co to open mail client; use #scrollUp to jump to top.
- Form validation flows to test: required-field enforcement, client- and server-side email validation, success and error response messages, and clearing/re-population after submit.
- Edge: invalid email formats, empty or whitespace-only fields, overly long inputs (subject/message), non‑ASCII/unicode/emojis, HTML/JS injection attempts in inputs, and malformed input characters.
- Edge: duplicate subscription attempts and idempotency (already-subscribed handling).
- Edge: rapid double-click or repeated form submissions (debounce/rate-limit), and partial network failures (timeouts, 5xx responses).
- Edge: JavaScript disabled or blocked — ensure graceful degradation (links and mailto still work, form may fail).
- Edge: accessibility and focus/keyboard navigation for inputs, subscribe button, and #scrollUp.
- Edge: expected UI messages missing or ambiguous (no confirmation, silent failure) and inconsistent element IDs (#susbscribe_email typo).

page_6.title: Automation Exercise - Polo Products
page_6.summary:
- Main purpose: a brand-specific product listing (Polo) for browsing items, viewing product details, and adding products to the shopping cart.  
- Primary navigation flows: header links (Home, Products, Cart, Signup/Login, Contact), category filters (WOMEN/MEN/KIDS and subcategories), brand sidebar filter (POLO, H&M, etc.), product actions (View Product, Add to cart), and View Cart.  
- Product-detail flow: click "View Product" → view details page → add to cart from detail page.  
- Quick-add flow: "Add to cart" from listing → expects immediate cart update/UI confirmation and option to "View Cart".  
- Account flow: Signup/Login accessible from header (affects checkout/cart persistence).  
- Important edge cases: adding same item repeatedly/double-clicking Add to cart (quantity/duplicates), out-of-stock or unavailable products, inconsistent brand counts vs displayed items, cart persistence after logout/session expiry or across devices.  
- UI/async edge cases: network failures or slow responses when adding to cart, missing/failed modals or confirmations, buttons not actionable on mobile/responsive layouts.  
- Navigation/link edge cases: broken links (Products/Test Cases/API Testing/Video Tutorials), pagination or lazy-load issues when many items, and mismatches between listing and product-detail data (price, SKU, images).

page_7.title: Automation Exercise - Product Details
page_7.summary:
- Main purpose: display detailed information for a single product (product_details/1) and let the user review the product and manage shopping-cart-related actions (View Cart, Continue Shopping) while navigating site categories/brands.

- Main user flows: navigate via top menu (Home, Products, Cart, Signup/Login, Test Cases, API Testing, Video Tutorials, Contact us), browse category/brand filters (WOMEN/MEN/KIDS and brand counts), read/write product review (WRITE YOUR REVIEW), and perform cart actions (View Cart, Continue Shopping, possibly add quantity/checkout).

- Important edge cases to test: submitting review while logged out or with malicious/special-character input (XSS/validation), submitting empty/invalid review fields, adding invalid or very large quantities to cart, out-of-stock or variant-not-available states, broken/incorrect navigation links or counts (brand numbers), cart/session persistence across tabs and after logout, responsiveness/scrollUp behavior on small screens and slow network/timeouts.

page_8.title: Automation Practice Website for UI Testing - Test Cases
page_8.summary:
1) Purpose: A catalog page that lists/links individual UI test cases for the Automation Exercise demo site — intended for testers to open and run specific scenarios (register, login, cart, orders, search, etc.).  
2) Primary navigation: top nav (Home, Products, Cart, Signup/Login, Test Cases, API Testing, Video Tutorials, Contact us) to move across site sections.  
3) Primary user flows exposed by links: open specific test-case pages (Test Case 1–20), user registration, login/logout, contact-us form, product search, view categories/brands, add/remove products to cart, place orders, newsletter subscription, verify product details/quantity.  
4) Secondary flows: opening external/internal resources (API Testing), watching tutorials, and returning to Home.  
5) Important edge cases — broken/truncated/duplicate items: many test-case labels appear truncated or duplicated (e.g., Test Case 10/11, clipped titles) so verify link targets and uniqueness.  
6) Edge cases — link behavior: links may be missing hrefs, lead to wrong pages, open in new tab unexpectedly, or be anchor-only; check 404s and redirect loops.  
7) Edge cases — auth/state: flows that require login should enforce auth, preserve/clear cart on logout, handle session expiry and browser back/forward.  
8) Edge cases — forms and inputs: validate empty/invalid inputs, large payloads, punctuation/HTML (XSS), duplicate accounts, CAPTCHA/ratelimit handling, and email validation.  
9) Edge cases — UI/responsiveness/accessibility: truncated text visibility, keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, and mobile viewport/cross-browser rendering.

page_9.title: AutomationExercise - YouTube
page_9.summary:
- Main purpose: A YouTube channel page for AutomationExercise that showcases the channel brand, links (automationexercise.com), and a list/grid of video thumbnails and titles for browsing and playback.
- Main user flows: navigate back to YouTube via logo, open channel/website via endpoint link, browse and paginate/infinite-scroll video list, click a thumbnail/title to open/play a video, and sign in or subscribe using the "Sign in" control.
- Key interactive elements to validate: #logo, #endpoint (external site), #channel-thumbnail, video thumbnails (with duration/Now playing overlay), and video titles.
- Playback flow specifics: open video detail page, ensure correct title/thumbnail maps to selected video, verify player loads and plays.
- Authorization flows: behavior when signed out vs signed in (subscribe/comment/watch history behavior).
- Loading and pagination: lazy-load/infinite scroll, placeholders, and ordering (newest first).
- Edge cases: missing/failed thumbnails or titles, truncated titles, broken external link (automationexercise.com), slow network/timeouts, blocked third-party scripts (player fail), and restricted videos (age/region/content).
- Responsive/accessibility: layout changes on small screens, keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, and screen-reader readability.
- State/consistency: inconsistent metadata between listing and video page, duplicated items, and intermittent 404s on click.

coverage_summary: The test cases cover navigation flows from the Home page to key pages such as Products, Cart, Signup/Login, API Testing, and Contact Us. Additionally, navigation from the Products page to specific brand and product details pages is tested. The Video Tutorials page is also covered via the Contact Us page. Notable gaps include testing form submissions, user authentication, and interactions with dynamic content.
